articles.title: Bombay HC directs internal audit of Kanjurmarg waste facility; seeks citizen participation is waste segregation
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Observing that an internal audit of the dumping facility at Kanjurmarg was lacking, the Bombay high court has directed a monitoring committee to
articles.body: MUMBAI: Observing that an internal audit of the dumping facility at Kanjurmarg was lacking, the Bombay high court has directed a monitoring committee to undertake one to assess how its functioning can be improved and to suggest immediate improvements to effectively address citizens’ grievances of odour, public health risks and what it said was the biggest challenge to ecology—plastics.Appreciating BMC's appeal to segregate wet and dry waste, HC division bench of Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said, "If citizens adopt an appropriate approach...it would go a long way towards addressing the urgent problems faced by citizens at large.''With over 7,000 metric tonnes of daily waste available, it is imperative to convert it for beneficial use including power generation, HC said in a November 18 order, out on Friday night.The HC addressed ongoing pollution and odour issues at BMC’s Kanjurmarg waste management facility calling for technological improvements, waste segregation at source, and development of a comprehensive policy for slum areas. The order, which included photos from a recent site visit by the Judges, emphasized the need for effective waste management, plastic ban enforcement, and AI enabled technological solutions to reduce environmental harm and protect public health.Authorities must urgently implement and pilot systematic segregation of wet and dry waste at the point of generation—especially in challenging wards—to reduce operational burdens and facilitate effective processing, the HC said and directed the committee and municipal corporation to consider advanced waste management technologies, such as converting waste to energy and possibly employing incineration, and to evaluate a potential ban on single-use plastics.The HC order seeking to establish lasting improvements for the city’s waste management framework, also directed the State to form a high-level committee to scientifically address garbage management in slum areas, which generate about 50% of Mumbai’s total waste, and to frame new norms for enforcing civic discipline in these zones.The HC order came in petitions filed by Kannamwar Co-op Housing Society Association and Sanjay Yelve highlighting health concerns due to the site’s proximity. On November 3, the HC had flagged “two fundamental issues” of the odour and lack of segregation wet and dry waste at the Kanjurmarg site.The HC said it appreciated innovative steps taken by the BrihanMumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to improve public health, hygiene and cleanliness and installation of AI enabled CCTV cameras but added “However, what disturbed us was that the operations at the Kanjurmarg facility continued to generate odour and pollution, which had been the subject matter of persistent complaints of the large population residing in the areas surrounding the Kanjurmarg facility.”“These areas include Vikhroli, Bhandup, Mulund, etc. and the lakhs of residents being adversely affected by such menace,’’ the HC said.The waste includes regular domestic household waste and that from municipal markets, like meat, vegetable markets apart from tonnes of plastic articles of every kind, cloth, cans, bottles, household sanitary waste, etc. are also received at the site said the HC. “The herculean efforts involved in segregation activity being undertaken at the site are beyond dispute,’’ the HC observed after hearing counsel Abhijit Rane for residents, amicus curiage senior counsel Sharan Jagtiani, senior counsel Anil Sakhare for BMC, Jaya Bagwe for MPCB, Saket Mone for the facility operator and AGP Jyoti Chavan for State but said the “major source of odour is the process of segregating and removing dry waste from the wet waste.’’The HC posted the matter to December 7 for further hearing including the internal audit to be undertaken by the monitoring committee.The issues HC flagged· Need for Waste Segregation at Source: Lack of segregation of wet and dry waste at the collection source is a major factor causing operational challenges and odour at the facility. The court emphasized that effective waste segregation at source would resolve many issues and improve waste processing efficiency.· Large Contribution from Slum Areas: Slum areas account for around 50% of Mumbai’s total garbage generation. The court found current legal provisions inadequate to ensure proper health and hygiene in these zones and recommended formulating robust policies and norms for slum waste management.· Proactive Steps and Public Sensitization: Initiatives such as installing AI-enabled CCTVs and publishing public appeals for responsible waste management were recognized. However, the court stressed the need to intensify citizen sensitization about not dumping garbage on streets and the importance of adopting systematic waste segregation practices.· Exploration of Advanced Solutions: The court recommended considering technological advancements (like incineration for power generation), evaluating a complete ban on single-use plastic bags, conducting an internal audit of the facility, collecting health data from medical practitioners in affected areas, and launching pilot projects for waste segregation in challenging city areas.Citizen Sensitization and Public Initiatives: Municipal authorities are instructed to intensify public awareness efforts about proper waste disposal, including screening educational films, running social media campaigns, and publishing advertisements. Compliance with segregation and management rules is set as mandatory, with penalties for violations.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Bangladesh violence: Fresh arson attacks reported as unrest continues amid Sheikh Hasina's return plans
articles.summary: Fresh arson attacks were reported across Bangladesh on Friday as authorities restored communication services in the hometown of former prime minister
articles.body: Fresh arson attacks were reported across Bangladesh on Friday as authorities restored communication services in the hometown of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina. The violence comes after several days of unrest over her planned return from exile.Hasina, 79, has said she intends to return to Bangladesh from India in December, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity. The sentence relates to a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising that led to her removal from power.The Awami League, Hasina's former ruling party whose activities are currently banned, had called for nationwide strikes this week to mark the anniversary of her death sentence.According to news agency AFP, Hundreds of paramilitary personnel have been deployed to control the violence, which has claimed at least three lives.On Friday, attackers hurled a petrol bomb at the residence of junior foreign minister Humaiun Kobir in Sylhet, a northeastern city, police said.Kobir warned that the government would respond strongly to such attacks."It is not possible to bring back a 'fled terrorist' by throwing petrol bombs," he told reporters.Hasina has repeatedly expressed her intention to return next month. In an email to AFP this week, she said she was "fully aware" that she could face execution by hanging.On Thursday, attackers set fire to the house of a former junior foreign minister from the Awami League in Rajshahi.In another incident, protesters armed with machetes set a police station on fire in Gopalganj, Hasina's political stronghold. Communication services in the area have since been restored.Police said 124 people associated with the Awami League had been arrested in the capital, Dhaka, over the past 24 hours. However, they did not provide further details about the arrests.The family residence of Nobel laureate and former interim government leader Muhammad Yunus in the port city of Chittagong was also targeted in an arson attack.Grameen Bank, established by Yunus, said more than 20 of its branches had been targeted in arson attacks during the current month.You use AI every day. articles.title: FBI most-wanted cartel boss El Chapo Isidro captured after gunfire at stadium; video shows fans panicking
articles.summary: A Mexican drug cartel leader listed among the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives has reportedly been captured by the country’s military, triggering violent
articles.body: A Mexican drug cartel leader listed among the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives has reportedly been captured by the country’s military, triggering violent exchanges of gunfire in Sinaloa state that sent baseball fans fleeing from a stadium during a match on Friday.Multiple Mexican media outlets reported the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro”, who allegedly heads the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organisation, also known as Los Mazatlecos. US Media outlet CNN said it was seeking independent confirmation from Mexican authorities and that the arrest had not been officially verified.The reported operation took place in Guasave, a city in Sinaloa known for its agricultural activity. Local authorities confirmed “an attack on federal personnel” in the city, according to CNN.The footage showed Mexican security force helicopters firing towards the ground while circling over Guasave. Gunfire also disrupted a baseball match at Kuroda Park stadium, where spectators were seen scrambling out of the stands.People could be heard shouting, “Get down, duck down, down, down!” as fans climbed over barriers. An official broadcast showed players from Venados de Mazatlán and Algodoneros de Guasave leaving the field midway through the game.“It’s being suspended… there’s a situation happening off the field,” the announcers said during the broadcast. “We wish first and foremost to ask God that everything is OK… there is a national security incident, it may be better for us to go to break now.”The FBI lists Meza-Flores as an alleged leader of a heavily armed drug-trafficking organisation based in Sinaloa. Its wanted notice accuses him and his network of trafficking heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the United States. The US government is offering a reward of up to $5 million for information leading to his arrest or conviction.“Known as El Chapo Isidro, he’s accused of spending the last 20 years flooding the U.S. with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin, and other deadly drugs, first as an independent drug trafficker and later as the head of the Meza-Flores cartel,” Acting FBI Director Driscoll said.Driscoll added that the organisation was also accused of crimes “ranging from kidnapping and extortion to torture and murder”.Meza-Flores was first indicted in a US federal court in 2012. A superseding indictment and arrest warrant were issued on November 26, 2019, charging him with multiple drug-trafficking violations and firearm possession.You use AI every day. articles.title: Friend to Trump, 'killer' for Ukraine: Zelenskyy hits back as winds of winter looms
articles.summary: Trump may call Vladimir Putin a \"friend\", but Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in no mood to share that sentiment.
articles.body: Trump may call Vladimir Putin a "friend", but Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is in no mood to share that sentiment.Taking a sharp swipe at the US president's warm description of the Russian leader, President Zelenskyy called Putin an "enemy" and a "killer", making clear that while Washington may see a friend in Moscow, Ukrainians continue to see the man behind a devastating war that has killed thousands and ravaged their country.Speaking to CNN, Zelenskyy said it was up to Trump "how to call Putin", but stressed that for Ukrainians, the Russian president remained an enemy."For us, he is an enemy... for us, he's a killer," Zelenskyy said, adding that Putin continued killing people "each day and night". He also suggested that Trump's friendly remarks towards the Russian leader were sending the wrong message to Moscow, arguing that Putin "doesn't feel enough pressure".Zelenskyy's remarks came after Trump referred to Putin as his "friend" ahead of a historic trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and the Russian leader in China on Thursday.Trump said he and Putin had shared a "great relationship for many years", signalling his continued personal warmth towards the Russian president despite Moscow's ongoing war against Ukraine.The trilateral meeting between Trump, Putin and Xi Jinping has drawn particular attention as the Russian leader continues to face international criticism over the invasion of Ukraine.For Zelensky, however, Trump's public show of warmth towards Putin raises concerns about the pressure being exerted on Moscow to end the war. He argued that treating Putin as a friend only makes the Russian president feel less pressure to change course.Trump, however, has maintained that his relationship with Putin could help bring the war to an end.Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday, he said the Russian president would "love to end the war" and claimed both Putin and Zelenskyy wanted the conflict to stop. Defending his remarks, Trump again described Putin as his friend, although he said he "can't speak" to whether the Russian leader was a friend to the United States.Winter is coming, and Russia's attacks threaten to make it harsher for UkraineAs the winds of winter begin to sweep across Ukraine, Russia's relentless bombardment threatens to make the coming months even more brutal for a country already battered by nearly five years of war.With temperatures set to fall, continued attacks on critical infrastructure risk deepening the hardship for civilians, raising concerns over how Ukraine will cope with another winter under Russian assault. The latest wave of Russian strikes has added to those fears, with missiles and drones targeting key transport links and residential areas across the country.Russia launched a massive overnight assault involving more than 400 drones and 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, targeting several parts of Ukraine.At least nine people were killed in the strikes, which hit bridges in the capital Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine. Zelenskyy described the bombardment as the biggest Russian attack of the year, as Moscow intensified its assault just days after Ukrainian forces badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge.Beyond the immediate casualties, the repeated strikes have also raised concerns over Ukraine's energy infrastructure as the country heads into winter.Attacks on power generation facilities, electricity networks and heating systems could leave millions vulnerable to freezing temperatures, particularly as repair crews struggle to restore damaged infrastructure amid continued Russian bombardment.For Kyiv, protecting the country's energy grid will be critical to ensuring that homes, hospitals and essential services can continue functioning through the winter months.You use AI every day. articles.title: 1 city, 2 very different airfare trends: Flights to Ahmedabad become 74.8% costlier in 7 months, while tickets out rise just 14.7%; Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Hyderabad routes record India's steepest hikes
articles.summary: Every other city in our tracker moves roughly in step in both directions. Ahmedabad has pulled apart for seven months and the gap is still widening.
articles.body: Every other city in our tracker moves roughly in step in both directions. Ahmedabad has pulled apart for seven months and the gap is still widening.One city is not behaving like the othersSince late April we have recorded the fare on 54 routes between India's eight biggest cities, every single day.Across that period the typical route has become 21.8 per cent dearer. Most cities have risen fairly evenly whichever way you are travelling.Ahmedabad has not. Flights into the city are up 74.8 per cent. Flights out are up 14.7.That 60-point gap is the largest in the country by a wide margin. The next widest is Kolkata at 13.7 points.The four steepest risers in India all end in AhmedabadMumbai to Ahmedabad is up 86.2 per cent. Delhi to Ahmedabad, 85.7. Chennai to Ahmedabad, 74.9. Hyderabad to Ahmedabad, 74.8.Travel the other way on the same routes and the increases are a fraction of that.It is not a one-off spikeThis first showed up in our July data and could have been a single event, a conference or a closure somewhere.It was not. The inbound index has climbed every month since: 100 in April, 110 by June, 127 by August, 138 in October and 150 this month.Outbound has risen too, but more slowly, and it spent June below its April level.What would explain itA one-way fare gap that lasts seven months usually means one of two things: more people want to get to a city than leave it, or there are fewer seats going in than coming out.Our schedule data showed Ahmedabad routes among the few in the country losing flights earlier this year, with Akasa Air and SpiceJet both cutting frequencies on the Mumbai leg.Fewer seats into a city whose inbound demand is holding would produce exactly this pattern.We are not able to confirm the demand side from fare data alone. What the data does establish is that this is now a seven-month trend rather than an incident, and that it is specific to one city and one direction.What it means for youIf you are flying to Ahmedabad, the booking advice that applies elsewhere applies here with more force. The inbound leg is where the increase sits, so book it early and book it separately from the return if that gets you a better price.If you are flying out of Ahmedabad, you are travelling on one of the better-value legs in the country right now.The short versionFares into Ahmedabad are up 74.8 per cent since April. Fares out are up 14.7. No other city in the tracker shows a gap anything like it.The four steepest-rising routes in India all end in Ahmedabad. Mumbai to Ahmedabad is up 86.2 per cent.It has widened every month for seven months, so it is a trend rather than a one-off event.Book the inbound leg early. The outbound is among the better-value flights in the country.About this dataDirection matters here. A route in this tracker is measured one way, so Mumbai to Ahmedabad and Ahmedabad to Mumbai are two separate routes with two separate fares.The Airline Fare Tracker records the median fare shown on Google Flights for 54 routes between Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad and Pune. Fares are captured every day, and this analysis covers 204 consecutive days from 28 April to 17 November 2026 with no missing dates.The index sets every route to 100 on 28 April and weights routes by monthly scheduled seats.Limits. These are advertised medians, not fares finally paid. All eight cities are metros, so smaller routes are not measured. There is no year-earlier comparison yet, so changes across the period cannot be separated from seasonal demand or from the fuel-driven capacity reduction that sits inside it.Roughly 6 per cent of daily readings were filled in by the data provider where a capture failed. The tracker records which airline flies a route but not which airline charged a given fare.TOI-DPA Airline Price Index is a joint initiative of The Times of India and Decimal Point Analytics.Source: Decimal Point Analytics Airline Price IndexStay updated with the latest Flight Price Tracker news. articles.title: A Pennsylvania mother died in 2019 and left her home to her son, who died in 2023; the county then sold it for $109,000 after sending tax-sale notices to the dead mother, but a court ordered the sale set aside
articles.summary: A Pennsylvania appeals court has ordered the cancellation of a $109,000 tax sale of a family home after finding that county officials failed to
articles.body: A Pennsylvania appeals court has ordered the cancellation of a $109,000 tax sale of a family home after finding that county officials failed to investigate notices returned with the word "Deceased". The property in Garnet Valley had belonged to Bonnie Wilson, who died in December 2019 and left the home to her son, Kevin Wilson, through her will. Kevin also died in August 2023, just weeks before the county's September tax sale. However, the Delaware County Tax Claim Bureau continued sending notices addressed to his deceased mother and did not make reasonable efforts to establish who owned the property. In a November 19, 2026 decision, available on Justia, the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court reversed a lower court's ruling and directed that the sale be set aside.Mother left the property to her son in her willBonnie Wilson purchased the property at 5103 Poplar Street in Garnet Valley, Delaware County, in June 2017. She lived there until her death in December 2019, when the home passed to her son, Kevin, under her will. Kevin also lived at the property. The property subsequently became subject to delinquent real estate taxes for 2021 and 2022. According to the court record, the county's Tax Claim Bureau continued to treat Bonnie as the property's owner because its records at the Recorder of Deeds and Board of Assessment still listed her name.In 2022, the bureau sent a certified-mail notice about the unpaid taxes to Bonnie at the property address. The letter was returned as unclaimed and unable to be forwarded. The bureau sent another notice in July 2023, informing her of the upcoming tax sale. This time, the letter was sent by certified mail with restricted delivery. A postal receipt was returned with an illegible signature. Meanwhile, Kevin had died on or about August 7, 2023. His will was probated on August 24, and Kelli A Barth was appointed executrix of his estate.County sold the home for $109,000Despite the earlier returned correspondence, the bureau proceeded with the tax sale scheduled for September 21, 2023. In August, it sent a final notice to Bonnie by first-class mail. That letter was returned on August 29 with a handwritten notation stating "Deceased". This was almost a month before the scheduled sale.A deputy sheriff also reportedly posted the property and personally served Kevin with notice on July 24, 2023. However, Kevin had already died by the time the sale took place. The bureau nevertheless proceeded with the auction, and CJD Group LLC emerged as the successful bidder, purchasing the property for $109,000.After the sale, another notice addressed to Bonnie was returned with the postal notation "Deceased". During testimony, the bureau's upset tax sale coordinator, Janine Heinlein, acknowledged that this was the first time the office had any indication that Bonnie was no longer alive. She also admitted that the final notice sent before the sale had already been returned with the same notation. Barth learned that the property had been sold only on October 5, 2023, when she signed an agreement to sell it and her realtor informed her of the tax auction.Court finds county failed to investigateBarth challenged the sale, arguing that the bureau had failed to follow Pennsylvania's Real Estate Tax Sale Law. However, the Delaware County Court of Common Pleas rejected her petition, finding that the bureau had met its notification obligations. The dispute then reached the Pennsylvania Commonwealth Court.The appeals court focused on Section 607.1 of the Real Estate Tax Sale Law, which requires tax claim bureaus to make reasonable efforts to locate property owners when notices are returned without personal signatures or other circumstances raise significant doubts about whether the intended recipient received them. The court found that the repeated notices returned with the word "Deceased" should have prompted further investigation. The bureau could have contacted the Register of Wills to establish whether Bonnie's estate had been probated, whether ownership had changed and who was entitled to receive notice.Instead, it proceeded with the sale without making those enquiries. The court also rejected CJD Group's argument that the sheriff's personal service on Kevin was sufficient. Kevin had died more than a month before the auction, making that notification ineffective.Appeals court orders tax sale to be set asideIn its November 19, 2026 ruling, the Commonwealth Court reversed the lower court's decision and remanded the case with instructions to enter an order setting aside the tax sale. The judges emphasised that the responsibility for complying with statutory notification requirements rests with the tax claim bureau, rather than being determined by whether the property owner or estate representatives had been diligent.The ruling does not mean that unpaid property taxes can be disregarded. Instead, it establishes that a tax sale cannot stand when the responsible government agency fails to make the additional notification efforts required by law after receiving clear indications that its notices are not reaching the property owner. For the Wilson family, the decision means the $109,000 auction sale must be set aside, returning the dispute to the lower court for the required order.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: A Canadian couple invested $5,000 in a freeze-dried fruit business after getting bored with their breakfast routine; it made over $100,000 in its first year before expanding to 600 stores
articles.summary: A Canadian couple who began making freeze-dried fruit at home to improve their eating habits have turned a small weekend venture into a growing food
articles.body: A Canadian couple who began making freeze-dried fruit at home to improve their eating habits have turned a small weekend venture into a growing food business. Jenny Yue and her husband, Han Yue, invested approximately $5,000 to launch OHME! Foods, initially selling their products at farmers' markets in British Columbia. The business made over $100,000 in the first year and caught the eye of independent retailers, eventually growing to hundreds of stores. What began as a personal quest to find healthier breakfast choices has since turned into their full-time entrepreneurial venture.A $5,000 investment helped launch the freeze-dried fruit businessThe concept of OHME! The foods were born during the pandemic when the couple were juggling demanding work schedules with the responsibilities of raising their young son. “Disruption to our daily routines has impacted our eating habits and overall wellbeing,” Jenny Yue told Entrepreneur in July 2026.They wanted to make healthier choices so they decided to change up their breakfast routine. They replaced less nutritious meals with oats, yoghurt and fruit but soon found that eating the same combinations every morning became repetitive.Han then remembered eating freeze-dried fruit during his childhood. The couple began experimenting with the process at home, looking for ways to make their breakfast bowls more enjoyable without relying on overly sweet toppings.Their experiments started with strawberries before moving to other varieties. The results were well received by their family and friends, including their son, who became their first enthusiastic food critic.An October 2025 interview with Early Stage Journal explained that the couple were particularly interested in the texture, flavour and nutritional qualities of freeze-dried fruit. Freeze-drying retains more of the fruit’s original characteristics than conventional dehydration and results in a light and crunchy snack.They also found that the Canadian market lacked variety with many products depending on imported berries. This meant that they could offer more locally made options.From a small weekend stall to a growing customer baseIn 2023, the couple decided to test whether other people would enjoy their products. They purchased a freeze-dryer, experimented with different fruit varieties and rented a commercial kitchen to begin production.Entrepreneur says their first investment was about $5,000 for equipment, kitchen rental, and ingredients. Instead of launching a big facility immediately, they decided to sell their products directly to consumers at farmers’ markets.OHME! officially met its first customers at a farmers' market in July 2023. These early selling opportunities also helped the couple understand what shoppers wanted. They could observe people's reactions, answer questions and make changes based on direct feedback.Early Stage Journal revealed another unusual part of the company's beginnings. The couple initially tested their products through a temporary stall at Urban Machina, an e-scooter store in Vancouver. The shop's owners had made space available for a pop-up while repairing the premises after a vehicle crashed through its window during a break-in.The unexpected arrangement gave the couple an opportunity to introduce freeze-dried fruit to shoppers who were largely unfamiliar with the product. Customers began returning for more, while cafes such as The Federal Store and Mah Milk Bar approached them through Instagram about stocking their snacks.The couple had originally expected the venture to remain a weekend activity. However, the growing interest encouraged them to explore opportunities beyond farmers' markets.The challenges that came with moving into retailThe transition from selling directly to customers to supplying retailers required the couple to learn several aspects of running a food company.Early Stage Journal reported that the founders initially approached 10 stores around Vancouver to introduce their products but received rejections from all of them. Rather than abandoning the idea, they continued attending pop-up markets and building relationships with customers.The company also undertook a rebranding exercise. Originally called OATME, a nod to the oatmeal bowls that inspired the first products. But customers often assumed the company sold oat-based snacks.Eventually, in 2024, the founders changed it to OHME! which gave the brand a clearer identity. The rebranding also opened up further retail opportunities and collaborations.Another important change was the packaging. The duo initially tried using clear acrylic boxes but the fruit became mushy when exposed to the air. Then they moved to airtight pouches, which increased the products’ shelf life to 2-3 years, according to Early Stage Journal.The University of Victoria's August 2026 alumni profile also highlighted how much the founders had to learn along the way. Both Jenny and Han graduated in 2017 with Bachelor of Science degrees in Health Information Science. Their previous careers were in healthcare and health technology rather than food manufacturing.OHME! Foods has expanded into hundreds of storesThe company's financial progress reflected the growing interest in its products. According to BCBusiness, Jenny Yue was recognised in its 2025 30 Under 30 list for her work with OHME! Foods. The publication reported that the company's monthly revenue increased tenfold in less than a year, rising from approximately $2,500 to $25,000.Entrepreneur later reported that OHME! generated more than $100,000 in sales during its first year, despite relying heavily on weekend markets. In its second year, the business expanded from approximately 50 specialty stores to around 120 independent grocers, generating roughly $350,000 in sales.The product range also grew beyond the original fruit snacks. The company introduced freeze-dried yoghurt crunch products, combining fruit flavours with yoghurt in small, bite-sized portions. According to Early Stage Journal, the new product received a Good Housekeeping Best Snack Award.The University of Victoria's alumni profile, published in August 2026, listed Whole Foods, London Drugs, selected IGA stores and Save-On-Foods among the retailers carrying OHME! products.By July 2026, Entrepreneur reported that the brand had reached more than 600 retail locations across Canada, including Whole Foods Market, Urban Fare, and London Drugs. It had also developed direct-to-consumer and wholesale sales channels while building its presence in the US market.The growth eventually prompted both founders to leave their regular jobs.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Make Big Tech pay': EU eyes digital tax to fund €2 trillion budget, risks fresh Trump clash
articles.summary: Europe wants Big Tech to pay its bills for the next seven years, turning the world's largest digital companies into a potential source of fresh revenue.
articles.body: Europe wants Big Tech to pay its bills for the next seven years, turning the world's largest digital companies into a potential source of fresh revenue.The move comes as the bloc grapples with competing spending priorities, mounting financial demands and disagreements among member states over how much money should be spent.European Council President Antonio Costa proposed taxing the world's biggest digital companies on Saturday while unveiling a revised spending plan for 2028-2034. He also suggested cutting 204 billion euros ($224 billion) from the European Commission's original budget proposal as the bloc seeks to reach an agreement on its long-term finances before the end of the year.The proposed tax would make some of the world's largest digital companies contribute directly towards the European Union's common budget. The move reflects Brussels' push to find new sources of revenue beyond contributions from member states, particularly as the bloc faces growing demands for investment in defence, technology, infrastructure and economic competitiveness.Major American technology companies, including Google, Apple, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft, could come under scrutiny if the proposal takes shape. However, Costa's announcement does not specify the tax rate, the companies that would be covered or how the levy would be collected.What is the EU budget and why does it need the moneyThe European Union's long-term budget, formally known as the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), is a seven-year financial plan that determines how much money the bloc will collect and spend on common priorities.The European Commission had proposed a budget of nearly 2 trillion euros for 2028-2034, aimed at strengthening Europe's economy, security and global competitiveness.The money is used to fund a wide range of programmes, including agricultural support for farmers, regional development, infrastructure, scientific research, education, climate initiatives, border security and defence. It also supports European industries, technological innovation and development partnerships with countries outside the bloc.Under the Commission's original proposal, 865 billion euros was earmarked for regional development and cohesion, while 409 billion euros was allocated to improving Europe's competitiveness through research, innovation and industrial investment. Another 200 billion euros was proposed for international partnerships.However, the proposed budget has faced resistance from several member states, which want to limit spending and reduce their financial contributions. Costa's suggested 204 billion euro reduction is an attempt to bridge these differences while keeping the bloc's spending priorities intact.Why is the EU proposing budget cutsThe proposed 204 billion euro reduction highlights a growing disagreement among EU member states over how much the bloc should spend and who should bear the financial burden.Wealthier countries, including Germany, Sweden, Denmark, the Netherlands, Austria and Finland, have pushed for a smaller budget and lower national contributions.On the other side, France and several southern, central and eastern European countries want to protect funding for agriculture and regional development. They argue that reducing these allocations could hurt farmers, rural communities and economically weaker regions that depend on EU support.The disagreement comes as the bloc faces pressure to spend more on defence, technological development and industrial competitiveness while managing demands for fiscal discipline. Costa's revised proposal seeks to strike a balance between these competing priorities and secure an agreement before the end of 2026.What does this mean for the USThe proposed tax could put American technology companies at the centre of a fresh dispute between Washington and Brussels, as many of the world's biggest digital firms, including Google, Apple, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft, are headquartered in the United States.If adopted, an EU-wide digital tax could increase the financial burden on these companies for doing business in the European market. It could also revive concerns in Washington that European tax and regulatory measures disproportionately target American technology firms.For US President Donald Trump, the proposal could become another point of friction with European leaders, particularly given his administration's previous criticism of EU actions against American technology companies. Any move perceived as unfairly targeting US businesses could complicate trade relations between the two sides.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Turns a blind eye': BJP takes swipe at Rahul Gandhi as Trump hails India's GDP growth
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP on Saturday took a dig at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, after US President Donald Trump praised India's GDP growth on
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP on Saturday took a dig at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, after US President Donald Trump praised India's GDP growth on Friday.Trump cited India's GDP while criticising the federal reserve for keeping interest rates high, arguing that the American economy could grow at 15 to 20 per cent if borrowing costs were lowered.Addressing a press conference at the White House, Trump pointed to India's economic performance as an example of how lower interest rates could support faster growth.Trump said India had managed to achieve "7 per cent GDP growth" despite having lower interest rates. He argued that the US, given its economic strength, should be able to achieve much higher growth if the Fed adopted a similar approach."If you look at India, they have low interest rates, and they have a 7 per cent GDP. We'd have a 14 per cent, 15 per cent, maybe even a 20 per cent GDP. It's really a sad thing when you do so great and then they (Fed) raise the interest rate. The fact is, we've blown through it," the US President said.Trump also accused the federal reserve of being "very political". He alleged that the central bank raised interest rates whenever the US announced strong economic figures, instead of lowering them to encourage further growth."Interest rates are too high because we have a very political Fed. I'm not blaming the chairman, but the fact that we have a very political Fed. Whenever we announce good numbers, they raise the interest rates. They do that for a reason. It should be the opposite," he said.He argued that stronger economic performance should give the US more room to lower borrowing costs. According to Trump, better financial figures indicate that the country is more creditworthy and should therefore benefit from lower rates."We do just the opposite. We do it to destroy the country. When we have these great numbers, you shouldn't keep raising the rates. You should lower rates because we're a better credit. We would have a GDP of 15 or 20 per cent, not 4 per cent. We'd pay off the debt very rapidly. That's the way it should work. But we do it in reverse," he said.The US President further argued that America should have the lowest interest rates in the world, given its position in the global economy."We're the country that makes other countries successful. Some of them are considered financial elite, but they are not. They are only elite because of us. So we should have the lowest," Trump said.His remarks come as US inflation remains above the Federal Reserve's 2 per cent target. The figures cited in his remarks put annual personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation at 3.6 per cent in September. Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, stood at 3.1 per cent.BJP takes jibe at Rahul GandhiTrump's reference to India's economic growth drew a response from BJP leader Ashish Sood.In a post on X, he said that while the world is recognising India's growth, the LoP has "turned a blind eye" towards it.He also responded to the US President's recognition of India's economic growth reflected the country's rising global standing and economic strength."US President Donald Trump’s recognition of India’s impressive 7 per cent GDP growth reflects the country’s growing global stature and economic strength.While the world acknowledges India’s remarkable progress, Rahul Gandhi and the Congress continue to turn a blind eye to the nation’s achievements," Sood said.From Trump's 'dead economy' economy remark to praiseTrump's latest remarks are notably different from his comments in July 2025, when he criticised India's trade policies and its ties with Russia.In a Truth Social post dated July 31, 2025, Trump wrote: "I don’t care what India does with Russia. They can take their dead economies down together, for all I care."He also announced a 25 per cent tariff on Indian imports and accused New Delhi of maintaining "far too high" tariffs and "the most strenuous and obnoxious non-monetary Trade Barriers of any Country".The remarks came after India and the US failed to conclude an interim trade agreement. Washington subsequently imposed higher duties and linked its decision to India's purchases of Russian oil and defence equipment.However, Trump had also acknowledged India's economic growth during a CNBC interview around the same period."You have a couple of countries, India is one, doing very well, but it's at 7, 8 per cent," Trump said, according to the interview transcript. He contrasted India's growth with that of the US and argued that the American economy should be allowed to expand at a much faster pace.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: South West birdwatchers describe thrill of starling murmations
articles.summary: Photographers and artists are encouraging people to watch winter starling gatherings.
articles.body:
Birdwatchers have described their joy at seeing starling murmations as a survey seeks to build a picture of their numbers.

Researchers from the University of Gloucester are updating a survey conducted a decade ago which examined the behaviour of the birds to find out what has changed.

Murmurations are lauded as one of "nature's winter wonders" as they involve masses of starlings swooping and diving in a pattern before roosting.

Encouraging people to participate in the survey, Devon artist Mike Langman said the dances were "just absolutely stunning", while Cornwall photographer Peter Glaser described murmations as "hair-raising".

The study hopes to find out if murmurations happen in the same places, if bird numbers have stayed the same and whether birds of prey are still around.

The 2014-16 study found there was an average of 30,000 birds in a murmuration, while some of the larger ones had more than 750,000 birds, based on sightings from 23 countries.

As part of the original study, researchers backed the idea that murmurations are primarily to protect birds against predators such as peregrine falcons and sparrowhawks.

Langman, who leads guided bird tours, encouraged citizen scientists to join in "for the experience as much as anything else".

He nominated his best spots for murmations in Devon as Countess Wear, near Topsham, and Thurlestone and Slapton Ley in the South Hams.

"Not only do you see them, you hear them as well and sometimes you even smell them," he said.

He said the sounds could be "remarkable" as tens of thousands of birds twist and turn before roosting when they fall silent.

"It's just like someone has switched off a light switch," he said.

Photographer Peter Glaser, who has captured many murmurations at Roughtor on Bodmin Moor, said they were "absolutely enthralling" to see.

He noted numbers this year "seem to be quite a marked improvement" on previous years.

"The expressions of delight [from others], the hairs on the back of your head rising, it is incredible," he said.

Wadebridge-based photographer Adrian Langdon said starlings often gathered at Penzance rail and bus station and Marazion Marsh.

"It's one of the spectacles of the natural world... it's pretty special," he said.

Prof Adam Hart from the University of Gloucester, who is leading the survey, asked people to provide accurate estimates of the number of starlings in the group as well as recording any birds of prey.

"We may see fewer birds, we may see fewer murmurations. We don't really know and that's the point of doing the survey," he said.

articles.body: Hyderabad: Telangana irrigation minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy reiterated that Telangana would not surrender even a single drop of its rightful share of Krishna or Godavari waters and asserted that the Congress govt is committed to protecting the state’s water entitlements against any attempts to undermine its interests.Addressing a public meeting at Huzurnagar on Thursday, Uttam said Telangana’s water rights were non-negotiable and the govt was prepared to fight any move that could compromise the state’s interests through every appropriate institutional and legal forum.Drawing a parallel with the services he had extended as a fighter pilot of Indian Air Force on borders facing China and Pakistan, Uttam said he was committed to protecting Telangana’s interests with the same discipline, sincerity, courage and resolve.“Whether it is Krishna river water or Godavari river water, we are not prepared to give up even a single drop.
